Q: Select Python interpreter does not work in VSCode - Python programs still use the old interpreter A:

There will be .vscode directory in your workspace, open settings.json and update your venv path

"python.defaultInterpreterPath": ".venv/Scripts/python.exe",

After that disable Python Environments extension and restart or reload the IDE.
This worked for me.

Q: How to provide custom message in pytest-html-reporter A:

Yes. Recent versions of pytest-html-reporter can display custom messages in two ways.

First, upgrade to the latest version:

pip install --upgrade pytest-html-reporter

Using print() or logging

Captured stdout, stderr, and logging output are automatically associated with each test and shown through the Logs column in the Test Metrics table.

import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def test_dashboard():
    print("Dashboard opened successfully")
    logger.info("Dashboard validation completed")
    assert True

Do not use -s, because it is equivalent to --capture=no and prevents pytest from retaining stdout and stderr.

Use this command if you want messages displayed both in the terminal and retained in the report:

pytest -v \
  --capture=tee-sys \
  --log-level=INFO \
  --html-report=./Reports/report.html \
  --title="Dashboard" \
  ./DASHBOARD/Tests/test_dashboard.py

--log-level=INFO is required for logger.info() messages; pytest normally captures only WARNING and higher.

Adding an explicit custom message

For a named text attachment, use attach_text():

from pytest_html_reporter import attach_text

def test_dashboard():
    attach_text(
        "Dashboard opened and validated successfully",
        name="Test message"
    )

    assert True

The message will be attached to that specific test and can be opened from the report’s data/attachments section.

Also, --self-contained-html belongs to the separate pytest-html plugin and is not required by pytest-html-reporter.

Full documentation and examples are available here:
https://prashanth-sams.github.io/pytest-html-reporter.github.io/

Q: How to get the steam AppID by AppName in Steam WebAPI A:

to get JSON of apparently all games in steam you can use https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreService/GetAppList/v1/?key=YOUR_API_KEY link. you may also want to add max_results=50000 param to make sure you get as many games as possible and include last_appid param, because number of games shown at a time is limited and the cap is approximately at 1.5 million app id so multiple requests are needed if u wanna get full list of games. for more info check - https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi/IStoreService#GetAppList but dont pay attention to the fact that the api link in the docs starts with https://partner.steam-api.com and not https://api.steampowered.com.

to get api key simply generate it on this - https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey website

this link - https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamApps/GetAppList/v2/ is deprecated so it doesnt work and this - https://partner.steam-api.com/IStoreService/GetAppList/v1/ is the link from docs but it doesnt work for me (seems like it works only for those who bought developer status for 100$) or i missing something

Q: How to use html test runner to generate html report in pytest? A:

HTMLTestRunner is designed for Python’s unittest framework and cannot directly run or report native pytest tests.

For pytest, you can use the pytest-html-reporter plugin:

pip install pytest-html-reporter

Then run your tests:

pytest tests/

By default, the report is generated at:

report/pytest_html_reporter.html

You can also specify the report location, filename, and title:

pytest tests/ \
  --html-report=./report/test-report.html \
  --title="PYTEST REPORT"

pytest-html-reporter generates a standalone HTML report and supports features such as screenshots, captured logs, attachments, test steps, analytics, archived build trends, coverage, reruns, pytest-xdist, and pytest-bdd.

Therefore, although HTMLTestRunner itself is not compatible with native pytest execution, pytest-html-reporter provides the equivalent HTML-reporting functionality specifically for pytest.

Docs: https://prashanth-sams.github.io/pytest-html-reporter.github.io/
GitHub: https://github.com/prashanth-sams/pytest-html-reporter
